mental_model: An SA maps a customer problem to a few well-chosen services, then justifies the tradeoff against the Well-Architected pillars. Know each service in one line, plus when not to use it.
verify_note: Technical audit: October 16, 2026. The cheatsheet prioritizes 13 P0 decisions; this glossary is reference material. Verify model terms, Region support, quotas, and prices against the linked AWS sources.

tiers.name: Tier 1: must know cold
tiers.note: Expect direct questions. Explain each in one breath: what it is, when to pick it, the trap.

tiers.name: Tier 2: should know
tiers.note: Comes up as follow-ups or inside a design. Know when it beats the tier 1 default.

tiers.name: Tier 3: recognize
tiers.note: Know what it is if the interviewer names it. Do not lead with it.

services.name: Region
services.what: A geographic area with multiple isolated Availability Zones.
services.pick_when: Choosing where to run: pick by latency to users, data residency rules, service availability, and price.
services.trap: Do not spread across Regions by default; multi-Region adds cost and complexity, so do it only for DR, latency, or residency needs.

services.name: Availability Zone (AZ)
services.what: One or more isolated data centers with independent power and networking inside a Region.
services.pick_when: High availability: run across at least 2 AZs so one data center failing does not take you down.
services.trap: Do not assume Multi-AZ protects against a full Region outage; that needs a multi-Region DR plan.

services.name: Edge location
services.what: A CloudFront and Route 53 point of presence close to users.
services.pick_when: Caching content and answering DNS near users to cut latency.
services.trap: You cannot run general compute or databases there; it is for caching, DNS, and light edge functions.

services.name: Local Zones
services.what: AWS compute and storage placed in a metro area, extending a Region.
services.pick_when: Single-digit millisecond latency to users in one city: media rendering, gaming, real-time trading.
services.trap: A regional deployment meets the latency requirement; compare prices, available services, resilience and operational cost rather than assuming one is always cheaper.

services.name: Wavelength
services.what: AWS compute inside telecom 5G networks.
services.pick_when: Ultra-low-latency apps for mobile devices on a carrier 5G network.
services.trap: Users are not on a partner 5G network, or latency needs are ordinary.

services.name: Outposts
services.what: AWS-managed hardware running in the customer's own data center.
services.pick_when: Data must stay on premises, or the app needs very low latency to on-prem systems, but the team wants AWS APIs.
services.trap: The workload can move to a Region; Outposts is a commitment with less elasticity.

services.name: EC2
services.what: Virtual servers with full OS control.
services.pick_when: Steady workloads, custom software, GPUs, or anything that needs OS-level control.
services.trap: Spiky, event-driven, or short tasks where Lambda or Fargate removes server management.

services.name: Auto Scaling group
services.what: Adds or removes EC2 instances by policy and replaces unhealthy ones.
services.pick_when: Variable load and self-healing; target tracking on CPU or request count, scheduled scaling for known peaks.
services.trap: Stateful single servers that cannot be replaced freely; move state out first.

services.name: Lambda
services.what: Runs your code per event with no servers; up to 15 minutes per invocation.
services.pick_when: Spiky, event-driven, short tasks: S3 uploads, API backends, queue consumers, glue code.
services.trap: Jobs exceed the invocation limit, require unsupported hardware, or cannot meet a measured latency/cost target. Compare containers for sustained utilization and test concurrency limits.

services.name: ECS
services.what: AWS's own container orchestrator, simpler than Kubernetes.
services.pick_when: Running containers without Kubernetes overhead, especially an AWS-only team.
services.trap: A real Kubernetes API/ecosystem requirement may favor EKS. Container portability also depends on identity, networking, data and AWS integrations.

services.name: Fargate
services.what: Serverless compute for ECS or EKS containers: no nodes to manage.
services.pick_when: You want containers without patching or scaling hosts.
services.trap: GPUs, daemon-style workloads, or large steady fleets where EC2 capacity is cheaper.

services.name: EKS
services.what: Managed Kubernetes control plane.
services.pick_when: The team already uses Kubernetes, wants portability, or needs its ecosystem (Helm, operators, Karpenter).
services.trap: Kubernetes adds operations without a customer benefit; evaluate ECS/Fargate or a supported app platform against team capabilities.

services.name: Elastic Beanstalk
services.what: Managed app platform: upload code, it provisions EC2, load balancer, and scaling.
services.pick_when: Simple web apps that need a fast start with little infrastructure work.
services.trap: Complex architectures that need fine control; use CloudFormation or CDK directly.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.what: Managed queue and scheduler for batch compute jobs.
services.pick_when: Large queued jobs: simulations, rendering, genomics, often on Spot.
services.trap: Interactive or request-response workloads.

services.name: Graviton
services.what: AWS-designed Arm processors for EC2, Lambda, RDS, and more.
services.pick_when: Cutting cost per unit of work for code that runs on Arm, which most interpreted and JVM code does.
services.trap: Software that only ships x86 binaries.

services.name: On-Demand pricing
services.what: Pay by the second or hour with no commitment.
services.pick_when: New or unpredictable workloads and short experiments.
services.trap: Steady baseline load; Savings Plans are much cheaper for it.

services.name: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances
services.what: A 1 or 3 year commitment in exchange for a large discount.
services.pick_when: The steady baseline you know you will run.
services.trap: Workloads you might shut down or move soon.

services.name: Spot Instances
services.what: Spare EC2 capacity that can be interrupted; notices normally precede stop/termination by 2 minutes, while hibernation starts immediately.
services.pick_when: Fault-tolerant batch, CI, stateless capacity mixed with On-Demand, and checkpointed training; react to interruption signals and design for notice loss.
services.trap: Databases or anything that cannot handle sudden interruption.

services.name: Karpenter
services.full_form: Karpenter (open-source Kubernetes node autoscaler, built by AWS)
services.what: Launches right-sized EC2 nodes for pending Kubernetes pods and removes nodes that are no longer needed.
services.pick_when: EKS clusters with varied pod shapes where fixed node groups waste capacity, or Spot-heavy fleets.
services.trap: It scales nodes, not pods. You still need HPA or KEDA to add pods, and disruption budgets so consolidation does not evict too much at once.

services.name: S3
services.what: Object storage designed for 11 nines of durability; versioning, replication, lifecycle rules.
services.pick_when: Data lakes, backups, static assets, ML datasets, logs; anything accessed as whole objects.
services.trap: Low-latency block storage for a database or a POSIX file system; use EBS or EFS.

services.name: S3 storage classes
services.what: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Flexible, and Deep Archive.
services.pick_when: Matching cost to access pattern; lifecycle rules move objects down as they cool.
services.trap: Infrequent-access classes for small or short-lived objects: minimum size and duration charges can cost more.

services.name: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
services.what: Moves objects between access tiers automatically based on use.
services.pick_when: Access patterns are unknown or change over time.
services.trap: Access is predictable; a plain lifecycle rule avoids the monitoring fee.

services.name: EBS
services.what: AZ-scoped block storage, normally attached to one EC2 instance; supported io1/io2 Multi-Attach volumes can attach to multiple instances in the same AZ.
services.pick_when: Boot volumes and databases on EC2 that need low-latency block storage.
services.trap: A shared POSIX file system is needed; use EFS or FSx. Multi-Attach requires application/filesystem coordination and is not a generic shared filesystem.

services.name: EFS
services.what: Managed shared NFS file storage; Regional file systems span AZs, while One Zone file systems store data in one AZ.
services.pick_when: Shared files for Linux fleets, containers, or lift-and-shift apps that expect a file system.
services.trap: Windows SMB shares (consider FSx for Windows), cheap object storage (S3), or assuming One Zone survives loss of its AZ.

services.name: FSx
services.full_form: Amazon FSx (Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS)
services.what: Managed third-party file systems: Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS.
services.pick_when: Windows SMB shares, HPC scratch with Lustre, or migrating NetApp workloads unchanged.
services.trap: Plain Linux shared storage; EFS is simpler.

services.name: Storage Gateway
services.what: Hybrid storage that presents cloud storage to on-prem apps as file, volume, or tape.
services.pick_when: On-prem apps need to keep working while data moves to S3, or tape backup moves to the cloud.
services.trap: One-time data transfer; assess DataSync or supported offline options rather than adding a persistent gateway.

services.name: Snowball
services.what: Physical offline data-transfer devices; availability and customer eligibility must be checked.
services.pick_when: Existing eligible customers with a supported offline transfer need; confirm current ordering eligibility before recommending.
services.trap: Assuming new customers can order Snowball; compare DataSync, Direct Connect, and transfer partners for current alternatives.

services.name: DataSync
services.what: Online transfer service that moves and syncs files between on-prem and AWS storage.
services.pick_when: Network migration of file data to S3, EFS, or FSx, with scheduling and verification.
services.trap: Database migration (use DMS) or bulk data over a constrained link; compare dedicated connectivity and currently eligible offline-transfer options.

services.name: AWS Backup
services.what: Central backup policies, schedules, retention, and cross-Region or cross-account copies for many AWS services.
services.pick_when: You need one auditable backup plan across EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and more, including copies to another Region for DR.
services.trap: A backup you never restored is a hope, not a plan. Test restores and measure the real RTO.

services.name: RDS
services.what: Managed relational databases with backups, patching, and failover options.
services.pick_when: Joins and transactions. Multi-AZ DB instance: synchronous non-readable standby for HA. Multi-AZ DB cluster (supported MySQL/PostgreSQL versions): writer plus two readable standbys across three AZs. Read replicas generally replicate asynchronously for read scaling.
services.trap: Massive key-value scale with simple access patterns (DynamoDB) or analytics over huge datasets (Redshift).

services.name: Aurora
services.what: AWS-built MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible database with storage replicated across 3 AZs, up to 15 read replicas, a Serverless option, and Global Database.
services.pick_when: High-performance relational workloads, fast failover, or cross-Region reads and DR.
services.trap: Small, cheap, steady databases where standard RDS costs less.

services.name: DynamoDB
services.what: Managed key-value/document database with conditional writes, regional ACID transactions, Streams and global tables.
services.pick_when: Known key-based access patterns at scale; design partition keys and indexes. Tables/LSIs support optional strong reads; GSIs provide eventually consistent reads.
services.trap: Ad hoc joins or treating capacity as a cure for a hot key. Transactions exist, but do not remove access-pattern or cross-Region consistency design.

services.name: ElastiCache
services.what: Managed in-memory cache: Redis OSS, Valkey, Memcached.
services.pick_when: Caching hot reads, sessions, leaderboards, rate limiting.
services.trap: As the only copy of durable data; use MemoryDB if you need durability with Redis APIs.

services.name: MemoryDB
services.what: Durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database with a multi-AZ transaction log.
services.pick_when: Microsecond reads where the in-memory store is the primary database.
services.trap: A cache in front of another database; ElastiCache is cheaper.

services.name: Redshift
services.what: Columnar data warehouse for SQL analytics at scale; Serverless option.
services.pick_when: BI and reporting over large structured datasets with complex joins.
services.trap: Transactional workloads or occasional queries on S3 data; Athena may be cheaper.

services.name: DocumentDB
services.what: Managed document database with MongoDB API compatibility.
services.pick_when: A document workload fits supported MongoDB APIs; test driver, feature, query, and behavior compatibility before migration.
services.trap: Simple key-value at massive scale (DynamoDB) or relational needs (RDS).

services.name: Neptune
services.what: Managed graph database (property graph and RDF).
services.pick_when: Highly connected data: fraud rings, recommendations, knowledge graphs. Ties to your GNN fraud project.
services.trap: Data that is not relationship-heavy; a relational or key-value store is simpler.

services.name: Timestream (LiveAnalytics / for InfluxDB)
services.what: Time-series services with different engines, pricing and customer eligibility.
services.pick_when: Evaluate the required engine and query model; LiveAnalytics is closed to new customers as of June 20, 2025. Consider supported Timestream for InfluxDB options for a new workload.
services.trap: Treating all Timestream offerings as interchangeable or recommending LiveAnalytics to a new customer.

services.name: OpenSearch Service
services.what: Managed search and log analytics; also a vector store for RAG.
services.pick_when: Full-text search, log analytics dashboards, vector search for retrieval.
services.trap: As the system of record; keep the source of truth in a database or S3.

services.name: Database Migration Service (DMS)
services.what: Migrates databases to AWS with ongoing change data capture to keep source and target in sync.
services.pick_when: Moving a database with minimal downtime; pair with Schema Conversion for engine changes.
services.trap: File or object data (use DataSync).

services.name: Aurora Global Database
services.what: One primary Aurora cluster that replicates to read-only secondary clusters in other Regions.
services.pick_when: Low-latency reads in other Regions, or a cross-Region DR target with a small RPO.
services.trap: There is still one writer. Write forwarding sends writes to the primary; fence the old writer before promoting a secondary.

services.name: DynamoDB global tables
services.what: Replicas of one DynamoDB table in several Regions that all accept writes.
services.pick_when: Multi-Region active-active access with key-value patterns and local-latency reads and writes.
services.trap: Conditional writes and transactions are regional. Cross-Region conflicts resolve by the chosen consistency mode, so do not rely on them for global deduplication of payments.

services.name: VPC
services.what: Your private, isolated network in a Region, with subnets per AZ.
services.pick_when: Control networking for resources such as EC2, RDS, and internal load balancers. S3 and DynamoDB are regional managed services accessed through APIs; a customer VPC is not required for every design.
services.trap: Adding VPC attachment to Lambda without a private-resource requirement; plan non-overlapping CIDRs and endpoint/egress paths when a VPC is needed.

services.name: Public and private subnets
services.what: A subnet is public if its route table points to an Internet Gateway, private otherwise.
services.pick_when: Load balancers in public subnets; app servers and databases in private ones.
services.trap: Putting databases or app servers in public subnets.

services.name: Internet Gateway
services.what: Lets resources in public subnets reach and be reached from the internet.
services.pick_when: Any VPC that serves public traffic.
services.trap: Private-only workloads; use VPC endpoints and NAT instead.

services.name: NAT Gateway
services.what: Lets private subnets make outbound internet connections without accepting inbound ones.
services.pick_when: Private instances need patches or external APIs.
services.trap: Heavy traffic to S3 or DynamoDB; gateway endpoints are free and skip NAT data charges.

services.name: Security group
services.what: Stateful virtual firewall on an instance or network interface; allow rules only.
services.pick_when: Default access control: reference other security groups instead of IP ranges.
services.trap: You need an explicit deny for a subnet; that is a NACL.

services.name: Network ACL
services.what: Stateless subnet-level firewall with ordered allow and deny rules.
services.pick_when: Blocking a known bad IP range for a whole subnet, as a second layer.
services.trap: As the main control; being stateless, you must allow return traffic explicitly.

services.name: VPC peering
services.what: A private one-to-one connection between two VPCs; not transitive.
services.pick_when: Connecting a few VPCs simply.
services.trap: Many VPCs or on-prem links; use Transit Gateway as a hub.

services.name: Transit Gateway
services.what: A regional hub that connects many VPCs and on-prem networks.
services.pick_when: Dozens of VPCs and accounts, plus VPN or Direct Connect.
services.trap: Two VPCs; peering is cheaper.

services.name: PrivateLink and VPC endpoints
services.what: PrivateLink powers interface endpoints for supported services; S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints are a different endpoint type.
services.pick_when: Compliance requires traffic to stay off the internet, or to cut NAT costs.
services.trap: Assuming endpoint reachability grants service permission or that every endpoint type has identical routing and charges.

services.name: Direct Connect
services.what: Dedicated private connectivity from a customer network to AWS; not encrypted by default.
services.pick_when: Predictable connectivity for hybrid workloads; separately design redundant connections and encryption using supported MACsec, VPN, or application TLS.
services.trap: You need it next week; provisioning takes time. Start with Site-to-Site VPN.

services.name: Site-to-Site VPN
services.what: An encrypted tunnel over the internet between on-prem and a VPC.
services.pick_when: Fast, cheap hybrid connectivity, or as backup for Direct Connect.
services.trap: You need guaranteed bandwidth and latency.

services.name: Application Load Balancer
services.what: Layer 7 load balancer: routes HTTP and HTTPS by path, host, and header.
services.pick_when: Web apps and microservices, containers, path-based routing, TLS termination.
services.trap: Non-HTTP protocols, static IPs, or extreme throughput; use NLB.

services.name: Network Load Balancer
services.what: Layer 4 load balancer for TCP, UDP, and TLS with static IPs and very low latency.
services.pick_when: Very high throughput, non-HTTP protocols, static IPs for allow-lists, PrivateLink services.
services.trap: You need HTTP routing rules; use ALB.

services.name: Gateway Load Balancer
services.what: Distributes traffic to third-party network appliances such as firewalls.
services.pick_when: Inserting inspection appliances transparently into traffic flows.
services.trap: Ordinary app load balancing.

services.name: Route 53
services.what: DNS with health checks and routing policies: simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue.
services.pick_when: Domain names, failover between Regions, weighted canary releases, latency-based routing.
services.trap: Expecting instant failover; clients cache DNS for the TTL.

services.name: CloudFront
services.what: CDN delivering static and dynamic HTTP content through edge locations.
services.pick_when: Global web delivery, origin offload, WAF, and TLS at the edge; uncacheable dynamic requests can benefit from edge connections and the AWS network. Disable caching for sensitive personalized paths.
services.trap: Non-HTTP protocols or a measured workload where added edge delivery gives no benefit; compare Global Accelerator for static IPs and regional routing.

services.name: Global Accelerator
services.what: Static anycast IPs that route users over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint.
services.pick_when: Non-HTTP or latency-sensitive global apps needing fast regional failover and fixed IPs.
services.trap: Cacheable web content; CloudFront fits better.

services.name: API Gateway
services.what: Managed REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs; features differ by API type. REST APIs support API keys and usage plans.
services.pick_when: Managed API authentication, authorization, integrations and throttling; compare the required features and cost of HTTP versus REST APIs.
services.trap: Usage-plan API keys are not authentication or authorization; use an authorizer, IAM, or supported identity integration. Quotas are best-effort, not a spending cap.

services.name: IAM
services.what: Users, groups, roles, and JSON policies that decide who can do what.
services.pick_when: Every access decision; follow least privilege.
services.trap: Long-lived access keys for humans; use roles and Identity Center.

services.name: IAM role
services.full_form: IAM role (AWS Identity and Access Management role)
services.what: An identity that is assumed and gives temporary credentials.
services.pick_when: Apps on EC2, Lambda, and containers, cross-account access, and federated humans.
services.trap: Never embed access keys in code instead of using a role.

services.name: Organizations and SCPs
services.full_form: AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies
services.what: Groups accounts; SCPs limit permissions for member-account principals without granting access.
services.pick_when: Multi-account setups: separate prod, dev, security, and billing.
services.trap: Assuming an SCP restricts the management account or service-linked roles; those are exempt. An applicable explicit deny still overrides identity-policy allows.

services.name: IAM Identity Center
services.full_form: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On)
services.what: Single sign-on for people across AWS accounts and apps.
services.pick_when: Workforce access to many accounts, federated with an existing identity provider.
services.trap: Customer sign-in for your app; that is Cognito.

services.name: KMS
services.what: Managed cryptographic keys and API operations with CloudTrail audit support.
services.pick_when: Control key access for service encryption and envelope encryption. Audit KMS API calls, but verify trail selectors and application data-event logging; not every local use of a cached data key calls KMS.
services.trap: Storing secrets like passwords; use Secrets Manager.

services.name: Secrets Manager
services.what: Stores secrets and supports configured rotation workflows.
services.pick_when: Credentials requiring lifecycle management; choose a supported managed rotation or implement and test a rotation function plus client refresh.
services.trap: Plain config values; Parameter Store is cheaper.

services.name: Systems Manager Parameter Store
services.what: Hierarchical storage for config and simple secrets.
services.pick_when: App config and feature flags; low-cost secure strings.
services.trap: Secrets that need built-in rotation.

services.name: Certificate Manager (ACM)
services.what: Manages TLS certificates; integrated non-exportable public certificates have no certificate charge.
services.pick_when: HTTPS on supported AWS integrations; exportable public certificates can support servers outside those integrations, with charges.
services.trap: Assuming all certificates are free or cannot be exported; check certificate type, integration support, and renewal deployment.

services.name: WAF
services.what: Layer 7 web firewall rules: SQL injection, XSS, rate limits, bot control.
services.pick_when: In front of CloudFront, ALB, or API Gateway for public apps.
services.trap: Network-level DDoS alone; Shield covers that layer.

services.name: Shield
services.what: DDoS protection; Standard is automatic and free, Advanced adds response team and cost protection.
services.pick_when: Advanced for high-profile public apps that cannot go down.
services.trap: Paying for Advanced on small internal apps.

services.name: GuardDuty
services.what: Threat detection from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs.
services.pick_when: Turn it on in every account to catch compromised credentials and odd behavior.
services.trap: Expecting it to block anything; it detects, other tools respond.

services.name: Inspector
services.what: Scans EC2, container images, and Lambda for vulnerabilities.
services.pick_when: Continuous vulnerability management.
services.trap: Runtime threat detection; that is GuardDuty.

services.name: Macie
services.what: Finds sensitive data such as PII in S3.
services.pick_when: Compliance audits of data lakes and buckets.
services.trap: Data that is not in S3.

services.name: Security Hub
services.what: Aggregates security findings and checks against standards across accounts.
services.pick_when: One view of security posture in a multi-account setup.
services.trap: Expecting aggregation alone to remediate findings; define owners and response actions even for a small account.

services.name: CloudTrail
services.what: Records supported AWS API/account activity for audit; management and data-event coverage differ.
services.pick_when: Forensics and compliance with protected central logging. Configure needed data events, such as S3 object activity, explicitly; Event history alone is not a complete audit archive.
services.trap: Performance metrics; that is CloudWatch.

services.name: AWS Config
services.what: Tracks resource configuration over time and checks it against rules.
services.pick_when: Proving compliance and catching drift, like an open security group.
services.trap: Tracking API calls; that is CloudTrail.

services.name: Cognito
services.what: User sign-up, sign-in, and tokens for your own apps.
services.pick_when: Customer-facing login, social sign-in, and securing APIs with JWTs.
services.trap: Workforce SSO into AWS accounts; use Identity Center.

services.name: SQS
services.what: Managed queue: Standard has at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO orders within each message group and deduplicates sends within a 5-minute window.
services.pick_when: Buffering spikes and retries with a DLQ. Use idempotent consumers: a crash after a side effect but before deletion can cause processing again, even with FIFO.
services.trap: Treating FIFO deduplication as end-to-end exactly-once side effects; use SNS fan-out for independent subscribers or Kinesis for replayable streams.

services.name: SNS
services.what: Pub/sub push to many subscribers.
services.pick_when: Fan-out: one event to many SQS queues, Lambdas, emails, or SMS.
services.trap: Durable buffering for a slow consumer; put SQS behind it.

services.name: EventBridge
services.what: Serverless event bus with content-based routing rules, SaaS and AWS events, and schedules.
services.pick_when: Event-driven architectures across services, reacting to AWS events, cron jobs.
services.trap: High-throughput ordered streams; use Kinesis or MSK.

services.name: Step Functions
services.what: Workflow orchestration with state, retries, branching, and human-approval waits.
services.pick_when: Multi-step processes like agent pipelines, document processing, order flows. Fits your S1 story.
services.trap: One simple step; a single Lambda is enough.

services.name: Kinesis Data Streams
services.what: Real-time ordered streams by shard that many consumers can replay.
services.pick_when: Clickstreams, telemetry, real-time analytics with multiple consumers.
services.trap: Simple job queues; SQS is cheaper and simpler.

services.name: Data Firehose
services.full_form: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose)
services.what: Managed streaming delivery to destinations such as S3 and OpenSearch, with optional transforms and buffering.
services.pick_when: Getting streams into storage with no consumer code.
services.trap: Sub-second processing or custom replayable consumers; choose a stream processor. Zero-buffering is available for supported configurations; dynamic partitioning does not support it.

services.name: MSK
services.full_form: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
services.what: Managed Apache Kafka.
services.pick_when: Teams already on Kafka, or needing its ecosystem and semantics.
services.trap: New simple streaming needs; Kinesis has less to operate.

services.name: Glue
services.what: Serverless Spark ETL plus the Glue Data Catalog of table metadata.
services.pick_when: ETL into a data lake and a shared catalog for Athena, EMR, and Redshift.
services.trap: Long-running heavily tuned Spark clusters; EMR gives more control.

services.name: Athena
services.what: Serverless SQL directly on data in S3; pay per data scanned.
services.pick_when: Ad hoc queries on a data lake; partition and use columnar formats to cut cost.
services.trap: Choosing a query engine by a blanket cost rule: benchmark sustained analytics against Redshift using concurrency, query performance, and total cost.

services.name: Lake Formation
services.what: Fine-grained permissions on data lake tables, columns, and rows.
services.pick_when: Many teams share one data lake with different access rights.
services.trap: A single team and a few buckets.

services.name: EMR
services.what: Managed Spark, Hadoop, and Presto clusters, on EC2, EKS, or Serverless.
services.pick_when: Large or tuned Spark jobs; migrating existing Hadoop. Maps to your Databricks work.
services.trap: Small ETL that Glue handles without clusters.

services.name: QuickSight
services.what: Managed BI dashboards, with natural-language Q and A.
services.pick_when: Dashboards for business users on top of Athena, Redshift, or RDS.
services.trap: The customer has standardized on another BI tool.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.what: Managed API to foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Llama, and others).
services.pick_when: Generative AI without managing model infrastructure. Verify the selected model and API retention terms, invocation logging, and inference routing before promising privacy or residency.
services.trap: A custom model architecture requires training or hosting control; consider SageMaker AI. Cross-Region inference can process data beyond the source Region.

services.name: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
services.full_form: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock (managed RAG)
services.what: Managed RAG: ingests documents, chunks and embeds them into a vector store, retrieves at query time.
services.pick_when: Answering questions over company documents with citations.
services.trap: Answers depend on live transactional data better fetched by a tool call.

services.name: Bedrock Agents
services.what: Agents that plan and call your APIs through action groups, often backed by Lambda.
services.pick_when: Multi-step tasks that need tools: the AWS-native version of your MCP connectors.
services.trap: A fixed workflow; Step Functions is more predictable.

services.name: Bedrock Guardrails
services.what: Filters for harmful content, denied topics, PII, and grounding checks on model input and output.
services.pick_when: Any customer-facing GenAI app, especially in regulated industries.
services.trap: Using content filters as authorization or access control. Guardrails do not replace IAM, document permissions, trusted retrieval filters, evaluations, or monitoring.

services.name: SageMaker AI
services.what: Build, train, tune, and deploy your own models; real-time, serverless, async, and batch endpoints.
services.pick_when: Custom models, fine-tuning, or full control of ML pipelines.
services.trap: Calling an existing foundation model is enough; Bedrock is faster to ship.

services.name: Amazon Q
services.full_form: Amazon Q (Q Business and Q Developer)
services.what: Generative AI assistants: Q Business over company data, Q Developer for coding and AWS help.
services.pick_when: Customers want an assistant without building one.
services.trap: They need a custom app experience; build on Bedrock.

services.name: Trainium
services.what: AWS-built chips for training models at lower cost (Trn instances).
services.pick_when: Large training jobs where cost per run matters.
services.trap: Code tied to CUDA-only libraries without porting effort.

services.name: Inferentia
services.what: AWS-built chips for low-cost, high-throughput inference (Inf instances).
services.pick_when: High-volume inference where cost per token or prediction dominates.
services.trap: Small or bursty inference; serverless or Bedrock may be cheaper.

services.name: Rekognition
services.what: Image and video analysis: labels, faces, text, moderation.
services.pick_when: Vision features without training a model.
services.trap: Highly custom visual tasks; train with SageMaker AI.

services.name: Textract
services.what: Extracts text, forms, and tables from documents.
services.pick_when: Invoices, forms, and scanned documents into structured data.
services.trap: Clean digital text that needs no OCR.

services.name: Comprehend
services.what: NLP service: entities, sentiment, key phrases, PII detection, classification.
services.pick_when: Standard text analytics at scale without an LLM.
services.trap: Open-ended generation or reasoning; use Bedrock.

services.name: Transcribe
services.what: Speech to text.
services.pick_when: Call center transcripts, captions, voice notes.
services.trap: Text input already exists.

services.name: Polly
services.what: Text to speech.
services.pick_when: Voice output for apps, IVR, accessibility.
services.trap: No audio output is needed.

services.name: Translate
services.what: Neural machine translation.
services.pick_when: Localizing content and support at scale.
services.trap: Legal or brand copy that needs human review anyway.

services.name: Kendra
services.what: Managed enterprise search with connectors to many document sources.
services.pick_when: Search across company repositories with access controls.
services.trap: A simple RAG app; Bedrock Knowledge Bases may be enough.

services.name: Augmented AI (A2I)
services.what: Routes low-confidence ML predictions to human reviewers.
services.pick_when: Human-in-the-loop review, like your S1 and S10 stories.
services.trap: Predictions that are always confident or always reviewed.

services.name: CloudWatch
services.what: Metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards; Application Signals adds SLOs.
services.pick_when: Monitoring and alerting on everything you run.
services.trap: Auditing API calls (CloudTrail) or configuration history (Config).

services.name: X-Ray
services.what: Distributed tracing across services.
services.pick_when: Finding which service in a chain is slow or failing.
services.trap: A single monolith where logs and metrics are enough.

services.name: Managed Service for Prometheus
services.what: Managed, Prometheus-compatible metrics storage and querying.
services.pick_when: Kubernetes and teams already on Prometheus. Maps to your Oracle work.
services.trap: Teams fine with CloudWatch metrics alone.

services.name: Managed Grafana
services.what: Managed Grafana dashboards over Prometheus, CloudWatch, and other sources.
services.pick_when: Teams that already use Grafana dashboards.
services.trap: CloudWatch dashboards already cover the need.

services.name: CloudFormation
services.what: Infrastructure as code in YAML or JSON templates.
services.pick_when: Repeatable, reviewable environments; drift detection.
services.trap: A different infrastructure-as-code tool is the established standard, or a short experiment does not justify a stack; drift detection covers only supported resource properties.

services.name: CDK
services.what: Infrastructure as code in real programming languages that synthesizes CloudFormation.
services.pick_when: Developer teams who want loops, types, and reusable constructs.
services.trap: Teams standardized on Terraform.

services.name: CodePipeline and CodeBuild
services.what: Managed CI/CD pipelines and build runners.
services.pick_when: AWS-native CI/CD with validation stages. Maps to your Jenkins toolchain.
services.trap: The team already runs GitHub Actions well; connect it to AWS with OIDC roles.

services.name: Systems Manager
services.what: Patching, run commands, Session Manager shell access, Automation runbooks.
services.pick_when: Operating fleets without SSH keys or bastion hosts.
services.trap: No fleet or AWS-resource runbook requirement exists; Automation can manage AWS resources beyond EC2, so serverless alone is not a reason to exclude it.

services.name: Trusted Advisor
services.what: Checks for cost, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits.
services.pick_when: Quick best-practice review of an account.
services.trap: Deep architecture review; run a Well-Architected review.

services.name: Cost Explorer
services.what: Visualizes and forecasts spend by service, account, and tag.
services.pick_when: Finding what drives the bill; requires good cost allocation tags.
services.trap: Alerting on overspend; that is Budgets.

services.name: Budgets
services.what: Alerts and actions when cost or usage crosses a threshold.
services.pick_when: Every account, so surprises surface early.
services.trap: Treating an alert or automated budget action as a guaranteed spending cap; billing updates and actions can lag.

services.name: Compute Optimizer
services.what: Right-sizing recommendations for EC2, EBS, Lambda, and more from real usage.
services.pick_when: Cutting over-provisioned resources.
services.trap: Workloads with too little history to judge.

services.name: Control Tower
services.what: Sets up a governed multi-account landing zone with guardrails.
services.pick_when: A new enterprise or migration needs accounts, logging, and guardrails from day one.
services.trap: A single-account prototype.

services.name: AWS Transform
services.full_form: AWS Transform (agentic migration and modernization service)
services.what: AI-assisted discovery, planning, and code modernization for migrations; AWS points new discovery use cases here.
services.pick_when: A customer starts a migration assessment and needs discovery and wave planning.
services.trap: Application Discovery Service closed to new customers on November 7, 2025. Confirm the current tool before naming one.

services.name: CloudWatch Application Signals
services.what: Application performance monitoring with service maps and SLOs on latency and availability inside CloudWatch.
services.pick_when: You want SLO-based alerting on AWS, the same idea as your Oracle Prometheus SLO work.
services.trap: An SLO without an error budget policy is just a chart. Agree what happens when the budget burns.

seven_rs.name: Retire
seven_rs.what: Turn it off; nobody needs it.
seven_rs.example: An old reporting server no one has opened in a year.

seven_rs.name: Retain
seven_rs.what: Keep it where it is for now.
seven_rs.example: A system with a hardware dependency or a recent upgrade.

seven_rs.name: Rehost (lift and shift)
seven_rs.example: A VM fleet moved with Application Migration Service to hit a data center exit date.

seven_rs.name: Relocate
seven_rs.what: Move the hypervisor-level platform without changing apps.
seven_rs.example: VMware workloads moved to VMware on AWS.

seven_rs.name: Repurchase
seven_rs.example: Your ERP story: Sage X3 to Sage Intacct, with a data migration.

seven_rs.name: Replatform (lift and reshape)
seven_rs.what: A few cloud optimizations without changing core architecture.

seven_rs.name: Refactor (re-architect)
seven_rs.example: A monolith split into services on Lambda and DynamoDB.

dr_tiers.name: Backup and restore
dr_tiers.how: Back up to S3 or AWS Backup in another Region; rebuild infrastructure with IaC when needed.

dr_tiers.name: Pilot light
dr_tiers.how: Data replicates continuously; core services are off or minimal until a failover scales them up.

dr_tiers.name: Warm standby
dr_tiers.how: A scaled-down full copy runs in the second Region and scales up on failover.

dr_tiers.name: Multi-site active/active
dr_tiers.how: Both Regions serve traffic; consistency and conflict handling determine write safety. Aurora Global Database is single-writer across Regions, even with write forwarding. All tier timings are illustrative targets, not guarantees; test end-to-end recovery.

dr_terms.meaning: Recovery point objective: how much data loss, measured in time, the business accepts.
Recovery time objective: how long the business accepts being down.
